propositions: The autouse _no_repo_commits guard invokes git rev-parse HEAD before and after every test, consuming ~207 runner-seconds or 75 projected wall-seconds across the 13,255-test suite on macOS.
A 895-test A-B-B-A measurement showed 9.3% median wall-time savings (5.04s) when the per-test Git subprocess guard was bypassed, while session-level dirty-tree detection remained active.

Replacing two per-test Git processes with in-process HEAD fingerprinting after one-time per-worker worktree discovery must preserve test attribution, the allow_repo_writes escape hatch, and session backstop integrity.

Survey of pytest, pip, Poetry, and pre-commit (4/4 consensus) showed no per-test source-checkout Git subprocess in their test hot paths, but no fidelity-preserving implementation primitive (Git library, hand-parsed refs, or guard removal) meets both consensus and rebar's stronger checkout-attribution contract.
